bug_semantics: Authenticated SSRF (CWE-918) in TaxHacker Email Sync: addEmailServerAction/updateEmailServerAction persist caller-chosen IMAP host and port with no allowlist, then testEmailConnectionAction and cron/manual sync feed those values into buildImapConfig (lib/email-sync/imap-client.ts). That helper copies config.host/config.port into the imap-simple connection object; fetchMessages and testImapConnection both call imaps.connect() and open INBOX, so the Node process opens a TCP (optionally TLS) session to any attacker-specified host:port, including localhost, RFC1918, link-local, and non-IMAP ports such as 6379. Failures surface as connection errors, enabling internal network scanning, service fingerprinting, and firewall bypass from a logged-in user.

potential_fix.approach: Before any IMAP connect (and before save/update of email-server settings), validate host/port: allow only ports 143/993, reject localhost and IP literals by default, resolve DNS and refuse private/link-local/loopback answers to reduce rebinding, then connect only to the validated target (as in unmerged PR #170 validateImapTarget).
potential_fix.rationale: The SSRF is the unauthenticated-to-the-internal-network TCP connect driven by caller-chosen host/port. Blocking non-IMAP ports and non-public destinations before imaps.connect removes the scanner/fingerprint path while still allowing public mailbox providers.
